messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: sustained 6x spike in /invoke tool calls across hosted cluster eu-west-1, tail p99 latency climbing from 120ms -> 1.9s, error rate creeping up to 4%. Auto-threshold triggered at 2245234567.
Devon: paging oncall. I see a big fanout from a few tenants, likely conversational agents hitting heavy tool-call loops.
Maya: @Devon I'm on it, jumping into traces now. Can someone pin the affected model versions?
Luca: quick grep on logs shows repeated agent invoke ids: agent.exec->tool.run with identical payloads from tenant: tenant-vec-42 and tenant-chat-91, starting ~2245234500.
Sam: running quick mitigation plan: 1) soft-rate-limit tool calls at edge for free tier 2) disable structured output streaming for all hosted endpoints 3) apply tenant quarantine for top noisy tenants. Propose to run commands now, will announce. :warning:
Devon: +1 do it staged: free-tier first, then 1% canary, then broader. Keep structured output off until p99 < 250ms.
ops-bot: EXEC: rbctl route update --region eu-west-1 --selector "tier:free" --inject-header "x-redwood-max-invoke:2" --dry-run=false (issued by Sam at 2245234578)
ops-bot: RESULT: rate-limit applied to 1k routes, expected reduction ~45% in invoke QPS.
Maya: turned on additional tracing: `TRACE=toolcall:verbose` for the canary slice. I'm seeing queued KV-cache thrashing in the runtime metrics.
Sam: applying tenant quarantine: `rbctl tenant quarantine tenant-vec-42 --reason "invoke storm" --duration 30m` (issued at 2245234586)
ops-bot: RESULT: tenant-vec-42 quarantined, routing diverted to fallback-model small-legacy for continued availability.
Devon: customer-impact check: Nina-cs, can you flag which customers are impacted and surface any high-priority contracts?
Nina-cs: tenant-vec-42 is a paid mid-market customer on dedicated? Actually they're on hosted Plus, impacted users see degraded structured JSON responses and reduced tool invocations. Opening a PM with status: investigating and mitigation in progress, ETA 30m.
Luca: runtime note: we see continuous batching backlog increase; dropping structured output reduces per-request CPU by ~18% in the canary.
Sam: action: disable structured output for hosted endpoints globally for 10 minutes: `feature-flag set structured-output false --scope hosted --expires 10m` (issued 2245234599).
ops-bot: RESULT: structured output disabled for hosted, telemetry event id 0x7f32.
Maya: monitoring p99, after actions p99 dropped to ~320ms at 2245234615, error rate down to 1.3%. Still above target but trending.
Devon: rolling to 10% of traffic reduction in invoke calls yielded expected drop. Next step: notify customers and prepare oncall handoff at 2245234680.
Sam: comms draft for status page: "We are mitigating an elevated invocation traffic event impacting structured outputs and tool calls. We have rate-limited free tier, quarantined noisy tenants, and temporarily disabled structured output to reduce latency. Engineers continue to monitor. Expected recovery within 30 minutes." Approving? :memo:
Nina-cs: approve, add note: impacted customers notified via email and support tickets, add postmortem request.
Devon: preparing handoff to night shift, summary bullets: what happened, actions taken, current state, next actions (1. monitor p99 for 30m, 2. lift structured-output flag when stable, 3. gradually restore tenant access after backpressure relieved).
incident-bot: Handoff scheduled at 2245234680 to oncall@rotation-night.
Sam: leaving final runbook note: command history saved under /ops/incidents/2245234567/invoke-mitigation.log. Anyone else?
Maya: adding diagnostic snippets to the incident folder and enabling a short eval run against canary to verify correctness once structured-output is re-enabled.
Devon: thanks team. Leaving channel for handoff.
ops-bot: DEPLOY-BOT: rolling fallback-model small-legacy applied to quarantined tenants (2245234698).
incident-bot: INCIDENT: status -> mitigated (ongoing monitoring).
